newsitem.title: USA: USDA begins new forward contract cattle report.
newsitem.headline: USDA begins new forward contract cattle report.

text.p: USDA's Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) began a new weekly report Friday on the number of new forward contracts for slaughter cattle in four regions of the United States.
The report, which AMS will issue around 1 p.m. ET each week, is part of a USDA effort to increase market information and to reduce the market power of big meat packers.
AMS plans to begin a second weekly report Monday giving contract cattle prices by grade and weight.
Friday's report showed 200 head of cattle for December delivery contracted in Colorado last week at 50 cents/lb under CME December live cattle.
There were no new contracts for October or November delivery during the week.
The report also showed 100 Holsteins for January and 100 Holsteins for February delivery in Colorado, both at $8 per cwt under February.
For March delivery, there were 400 Holsteins at $7.50 per cwt under April in Texas/Oklahoma and 100 Holsteins at $8 per cwt under April in Colorado.
For April, there were 300 Holsteisn at $7 per cwt under April in Texas/Oklahoma and 100 Holsteins at $8 per cwt under April in Colorado.
There was no activity in the week for the other two regions, Kansas and Nebraska/Wyoming.
